title: Marvel’s ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Won’t Screen for BAFTA, Golden Globes and Other Early Awards Groups to Guard Its Spoilers (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Marvel will skip early awards screenings for Avengers: Doomsday, curbing pre-release buzz and traditional awards campaigning.
content: Earth’s Mightiest Heroes will fight Doctor Doom in the latest Avengers installment, but they won’t face the first wave of critics and major guilds on the awards calendar . Marvel Studios ’ “ Avengers: Doomsday ” will not screen for awards voting bodies before its world premiere, Variety has learned exclusively, a move designed to protect its theatrical run by keeping the film’s closely guarded plot turns out of the spoiler ecosystem ahead of its Dec. 18 theatrical release. The film premieres Dec. 14 in Los Angeles, just four days before it opens nationwide. Related Stories Here's How to Watch WWE Crown Jewel 2026 Live Online WWE, Disney Team for 'Avengers: Doomsday'-Themed Worlds Collide, John Cena Classic The strategy follows a well-worn playbook for event films of this scale, from “Star Wars: The Force Awakens” to “Spider-Man: No Way Home.” But protecting the surprises comes at a cost, with “Doomsday” set to sit out a long stretch of the precursor season as voting windows close before most awards voters have seen a frame. The biggest question is: What does that mean for the Oscars ? The most consequential window belongs to the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences. Preliminary voting for the Oscar shortlists begins Monday, Dec. 7, and closes Dec. 11, with shortlists in 12 categories announced on Dec. 15, the day after the film’s premiere. Those categories are animated short film, casting, cinematography, documentary feature, documentary short, international feature, live action short, makeup and hairstyling, original score, original song, sound and visual effects. “Doomsday” could factor into as many as seven of them. Visual effects is where “Doomsday” has the clearest path because of how that race is structured, and the studio’s previous successes in the category (i.e., “Guardians of the Galaxy,” “Black Panther: Wakanda Forever”). title:
Billy Ray Joins Oscar Short Contender 'Magan's Fare,' Starring Barkhad
 Abdi, as Executive Producer
summary: Billy Ray joins as EP on Oscar-shortlisted short Magan's Fare, boosting the project's visibility for talent involved.
content: Screenwriter Billy Ray (“ The Hunger Games ,” “Shattered Glass,” “Richard Jewell,” Nicole Kidman’s AMC ad ), who penned the 2013 Oscar-nominated “Captain Phillips, has boarded the film “Magan’s Fare” as an executive producer. The new film stars Barkhad Abdi , the Somali actor who broke out in the Paul Greengrass film and earned a Best Supporting Actor Oscar nomination. Directed by Christopher Knoblock and Dana White, “Magan’s Fare” is vying in the Best Live Action Short race this year, having qualified out of the Raindance Film Festival where it won the top short prize. Next up, it plays HollyShorts UK. Related Stories Why Is the ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Trailer So… Gloomy? Internet Erupts Over Latest Look at Marvel Movie AI Film ‘Gods Don’t Give Gifts’ Deemed Ineligible by Academy for Best Animated Feature Oscar The 26-minute drama stars Abdi as Magan, “a Somali-born rideshare driver who takes an older woman, Jorani (Alexis Rhee), back to her nursing home, only to discover the facility has given away her bed. With his passenger suddenly displaced and no one else willing to take responsibility for her, Magan must figure out what to do next,” per the announcement. “The last two years have demonstrated on a grand level that small businesses need more help than big ones do,” Ray said at a recent Los Angeles screening of the film. “Well, in our community, small movies need more help than big ones do. I’m happy to be helping this small movie. I hope all of you will too. It’s so beautifully written, it’s so beautifully directed, it’s so beautifully performed. The music, the cinematography, all of it, just executed with such love and care, and integrity.” Knoblock and White added, “We are deeply honored to have Billy Ray join our ‘Magan’s Fare’ FYC campaign as an executive producer. title:
AI Film 'Gods Don't Give Gifts' Deemed Ineligible by Academy for Best
 Animated Feature Oscar
summary: The Academy ruled AI-driven film Gods Don't Give Gifts ineligible for Animated Feature, signaling stricter standards on AI.
content: “Gods Don’t Give Gifts,” an upcoming film from YouTuber Gossip Goblin that was made entirely with generated artificial intelligence, was deemed ineligible for the Best Animated Feature Oscar at the upcoming Academy Awards. As IndieWire previously reported on “Gods Don’t Give Gifts,” which is the first fully AI movie to be released theatrically, the film had submitted for consideration and had planned FYC screenings alongside its theatrical release on December 4. But the film was not included among the list of 38 animated films deemed eligible for this year’s Oscars that were announced Monday, November 23. IndieWire understands that the Academy’s Animation Branch Executive Committee determined “Gods Don’t Give Gifts” did not meet the Academy’s definition of an animated film under the rules for the 99th Awards . Related Stories The Best Visual Effects in ‘Wildwood’ Are the Ones You Can’t See — Watch From ‘Disclosure Day’ to ‘Devil Wears Prada’: Emily Blunt Breaks Down 10 of Her Greatest Movie Moments Here’s the full rule as written that the Academy felt “Gods Don’t Give Gifts” did not satisfy: An animated film is one in which characters or objects are given the illusion of life by having movement created for them, by any human means. While the crucial movement of a live-action motion picture is captured at speed, animation is the craft of human creation and manipulation of images to produce a performance from inanimate objects. At least 75 percent of the motion picture’s running time, without opening or end credits, must include animation of the primary subject or subjects. An animated feature has a running time of more than 40 minutes. Upon submission, filmmakers must provide information supporting how the motion picture qualifies as an animated film. title: ‘Ted Lasso’ Renewed for Season 5 at Apple TV, With Jason Sudeikis Returning
summary: Apple renews Ted Lasso for Season 5 with Jason Sudeikis, extending comedy-series employment and guest-casting opportunities.
content: Believe: “ Ted Lasso ” and the Lady Greyhounds are back for more. Apple TV announced Monday that it has given a Season 5 pickup to the hit Jason Sudeikis comedy from Warner Bros. TV. News wasn’t a surprise, given how well the Season 4 revival did for Apple TV; it just came down to striking a new deal with Sudeikis and Warner Bros. to continue the show. Sudeikis is back as star and executive producer. On a recent episode of the podcast “Talk Easy With Sam Fragoso,” Sudeikis expressed an interest in continuing “Ted Lasso” through Seasons 5 and 6, making for another three-season arc. According to Nielsen, the “Ted Lasso” Season 4 premiere pulled in 296.6 million minutes watched over the course of Aug. 4-5, making it the biggest launch in the history of Apple TV, above all previous seasons of the show and other buzzy Apple series. After the show’s original storyline wrapped up at the end of Season 3, “Ted Lasso” returned with a new storyline: Ted returning to AFC Richmond to coach a second-division women’s football team. Besides Sudeikis, also back were stars Hannah Waddingham, Juno Temple, Brett Goldstein, Brendan Hunt and Jeremy Swift, while the Season 4 cast also included Tanya Reynolds, Jude Mack, Faye Marsay, Rex Hayes, Aisling Sharkey, Abbie Hern and Grant Feely.  With 11 Mentions as 'Dune: Part Three' and 'La Bola Negra' Follow With Eight
summary: The Odyssey leads Critics Choice craft shortlists; Dune: Part Three and La Bola Negra follow, signaling strong awards momentum.
content: Universal’s “ The Odyssey ” leads the shortlists for the 32nd Critics Choice Awards ‘ below-the-line categories with 11 mentions. The Homer epic, the first feature shot entirely on Imax film cameras, landed on all 11 artisan lists, from Hoyte van Hoytema’s cinematography and Ellen Mirojnick’s costumes to John Papsidera’s casting. Its only absence came in young actor/actress, the lone performance category voted on by the committee. They arrive just ahead of nomination voting, which begins on Thanksgiving Day, when ballots go out to the organization’s more than 500 members. Each artisan category will yield six nominees, and best picture will recognize 10 films. The full membership also votes in every other major category, including acting, screenplay, animated feature and international feature. Warner Bros.’ sci-fi conclusion “Dune: Part Three,” which opens Dec. 18, and Netflix’s Spanish-language epic “ La Bola Negra ” follow with eight apiece. For the latter, Gris Jordana’s cinematography, Ana López Cobos’ costumes and Roger Bellés and Judit Ferrer’s production design all made the cut. So did composer and songwriter Raül Refree, for the score and for co-writing “La Nieve” with Guitarricadelafuente, who also stars. GKids’ monster movie “Godzilla Minus Zero” and Laika’s stop-motion “ Wildwood ” tied with seven. At the same time, Amazon MGM Studios’ “Project Hail Mary” and Focus Features’ “Werwulf” each picked up six. “Godzilla Minus Zero” picks up where its predecessor left off. title: ‘Only Murders In The Building’ Returning To New York For Likely Season 7
summary: Only Murders in the Building eyes a seventh season shooting in New York, signaling upcoming local casting opportunities.
content: A new murder mystery sent the characters from Hulu ‘s Only Murders in the Building to London for Season 6, and it’s where the show hosted its premiere this evening, with the cast, producers, and creatives teasing what’s ahead. The series will premiere on December 8 via Hulu and on Disney+ internationally. On the red carpet at London’s Leicester Square, John Hoffman , who co-created the series with star Steve Martin , told Deadline that although they had fun across the pond, the show will return to New York, should it get renewed for a seventh season. Deadline previously reported that the show’s writers room moved to New York after being located in Los Angeles for the past six seasons. Related Stories Cancellations and Renewals 'The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County' Renewed At Hulu For 20 More Episodes News 'Gilmore Girls: A Year In The Life' Gets New Home On Hulu After Netflix Deal Ends, Release Date Set “I love New York like nobody else, and the show is so steeped in New York. So, going back to New York is going to be a thrill for Season 7,” Hoffman said. “I do hope that might happen. And then, beyond that, we’ve learned a lesson from London, which is that the show can travel, and it really excites everybody to imagine where it might be able to go next.” Watch on Deadline ‘Only Murders In The Building’ showrunner John Hoffman confirms return to New York for Season 7: “I love New York like nobody else and the show is so steeped in New York. So, going back to New York is going to be a thrill for Season 7.” pic.twitter.com/c4Ir9pBslH Speaking of Martin, he shared his feelings about returning to the Big Apple alongside Martin Short . The usual trio was one down, with Selena Gomez unable to attend the celebration due to a scheduling conflict. “We’re always open to it [filming in new cities] but right now, our goal is to head back to New York City,” stated Martin. title:
Steven Spielberg Directing His First Western with Paul Thomas Anderson
 Writing the Script
summary: Steven Spielberg will direct his first Western from a script by Paul Thomas Anderson, creating high-profile casting prospects.
content: Steven Spielberg has directed musicals, sci-fi epics, adventure films, and biopics, but one genre has eluded him over the course of his decades-long career. He has never directed a Western, despite having openly longed to put his spin on the type of movies that turned one of his idols, John Ford, into a legend. Well, the wait is over. Spielberg is developing an untitled film for Focus Features about two fugitives charting a course across the American West, and he’s assembled a crack team to help him. The ensemble will include Jessie Buckley, fresh off her Oscar win for “Hamnet,” Cillian Murphy, the Oscar-winning star of “Oppenheimer,” and Mark Rylance, a frequent Spielberg collaborator who won, you guessed it, an Oscar for “Bridge of Spies.” Related Stories ‘Focker In-Law’ Review: An Eager Ariana Grande Isn’t Enough to Save a Comedy Sequel That Can’t Remember What People Liked About This Franchise Jane Fonda on Documentary ‘Gaslit,’ Trump, and What the Democrats’ Midterm Victory Means for Climate Change But there’s more to get cinephiles’ hearts racing! Paul Thomas Anderson , the Oscar-winning filmmaker behind “Boogie Nights,” “There Will Be Blood,” and “One Battle After Another,” is writing the script. It’s based on Kevin Barry’s novel, “The Heart in Winter.” Though Anderson usually directs his screenplays, he’s done script doctoring for Ridley Scott (“Napoleon”) and Martin Scorsese (“Killers of the Flower Moon” and the upcoming “What Happens at Night”). He also did some work on “Corky Romano” — hey, they can’t all be winners! So why not join Spielberg’s merry band? Spielberg is still one of the all-time greats, but he could use a hit . “Disclosure Day,” which marked his return to summer movies, was a box office disappointment, and his most recent films, like “The Fabelmans” and “West Side Story,” struggled to connect with audiences despite earning excellent reviews.  From Video Games

title: Designing a ‘Hunger Games’ Prequel: From Using 600,000 Flowers in the ‘Sunrise on the Reaping’ Arena to Recreating the Capitol in the 1970s
summary: The Hunger Games prequel uses vast practical builds, including 600,000 flowers and a 1970s Capitol, demanding immersive performances.
content: Production designer Uli Hanisch thought shooting the highly anticipated “Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” in the remote town of Asturias, Spain, meant they would be safe from spoilers. The production would shoot in a desolate valley, requiring an hours-long trek to the set, plus the lack of hotel accommodations and the occasional restaurant nearby, reassured him. Until it happened. “We had the experience from last time where fans were following us to Poland trying to take pictures, but up there, it’s nothing, it’s just us,” Hanisch tells Variety . “We were starting to build up the cornucopia pieces, and I think after two or three days, the first images appeared on the internet. It was somebody saying, ‘Oh, we found them.’ I was like, ‘How is that even possible?’” Related Stories WWE, Disney Team for 'Avengers: Doomsday'-Themed Worlds Collide, John Cena Classic Here's How to Watch WWE Crown Jewel 2026 Live Online Even though sleuthing fans were able to find it, the location is so secluded that Hanisch wondered if it would be feasible to get a crew of the necessary magnitude all the way up there. But once he saw the luscious greenery contrasting the jagged mountains, he knew they had found the arena for the Second Quarter Quell, and they’d have to make it work. “I stepped out of the car and looked into the valley and said, ‘God damn, yeah, that’s it,’” Hanisch says. “I sent an image to Francis [Lawrence, the franchise’s longtime director], saying, ‘Look, this is our valley, but it’s really far away.’ And he said, ‘Yeah, well, we have to do it here.’” The next step was designing and building the Cornucopia — the focal point of the arena, which distinguishes each iteration of the Hunger Games (and each installment of the film franchise) from the others. Similar to the paradoxical landscape, Hanisch and his team wanted to create something that balanced beauty with danger. title: Anya Taylor-Joy ‘Went Mute’ on ‘Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum’ Set When Ian McKellen Showed Up: ‘That’s F—ing Gandalf’
summary: New LOTR film underway; Taylor-Joy notes intimidating set with Ian McKellen, underscoring the franchise's high-profile collaborations.
content: Anya Taylor-Joy , who is set to play Seren, an elf, in “ The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum ,” says the last time she found herself starstruck was when she first came face-to-face with Ian McKellen as Gandalf on set. “I wasn’t prepared,” she told Dazed . “I went mute. And he’s the loveliest, funniest, most wonderful man and actor. But that’s fucking Gandalf!” While Taylor-Joy didn’t let much else slip about the highly anticipated film in her cover story, she told the outlet she had specifically hoped to land a role in a “Lord of the Rings” film. “I had called my agent earlier on ‘Dune,’ being like, ‘If they ever make ‘The Lord of the Rings,’ let them know that I’d be interested,’” she said. Related Stories UFC's Event Sellout Spree Powers TKO Q3 Earnings WWE, Disney Team for 'Avengers: Doomsday'-Themed Worlds Collide, John Cena Classic While McKellen originated the role of Gandalf in Peter Jackson’s “The Lord of the Rings” trilogy, a number of newcomers will make their franchise debut with “The Hunt for Gollum,” including Kate Winslet as Marigol and Leo Woodall as Halvard. Mainstays including Elijah Wood (Frodo) and Lee Pace (King Thranduil) are also set to reprise their roles. Andy Serkis pulls double duty, playing Gollum while also directing the film, while Jamie Dornan replaces Viggo Mortensen as Aragorn. Back in July, Taylor-Joy admitted to Variety she hadn’t yet read the “Lord of the Rings” books despite landing the role in the forthcoming film. “I’m about to read the books now, actually,” she told Variety ’s Marc Malkin. “So as a child, I had a misguided idea that you could only be a ‘Harry Potter’ fan or a ‘Lord of the Rings’ fan. Nobody told me that. I just came up with that on my own. Luckily, throughout COVID, I then watched all of ‘Lord of the Rings,’ and turns out you can love both, and you should.” Malkin also asked the actress about her reaction to getting cast in “The Hunt for Gollum” at the time, to which she responded: “It’s so fun. title: ‘Michael’ Director Antoine Fuqua Accused of Assault, Battery by L.A. Bar Manager
summary: Antoine Fuqua faces civil assault allegations, which could affect scheduling and workplace conditions on Michael and future projects.
content: “Michael” director Antoine Fuqua has been accused of assault, battery and intentional infliction of emotional distress by a Los Angeles bar manager following an incident back in February during which Fuqua allegedly pulled a gun on and struck the employee in the head. In a 10-page civil claim filed Friday in the Los Angeles Superior Court, William Rosenthal, an assistant manager at the bar Good Times at Davey Wayne’s, is said to have denied entry to Fuqua, his son, Brando, and his daughter because they were “visibly overly intoxicated.” Rosenthal was then spat on by a member of the group, to which Rosenthal told them they needed to leave the bar. title: ‘Clashing Through The Snow’ Stars Christopher Briney & Michelle Randolph Talk Comedy’s “Important” Presence In Script And How They Built Their Characters
summary: Leads emphasize comedy-driven character work and collaborative chemistry building, offering pointers for holiday rom-com performances.
content: In Prime Video’s latest original Christmas romantic comedy, Clashing Through the Snow , Christopher Briney ( The Summer I Turned Pretty) and Michell Randolph ( Landman ) portray rival editors whose relationship takes an enemies to lovers arc during a road trip to New York . Ryan Mitchell (Briney) and Hannah Hendricks both hear from their boss Jeremy (P.J. Byrne) separately that layoffs loom at Latitude Publishing, where they will compete for a merged version of their roles in the new year. The ambitious employees then both set up secret meetings with prospective authors that could respectively land them the job, but require travel to New York city over the Christmas holiday. The pair exhibit fundamentally different taste in books and what they aim to sell, but their shared love of reading provides them common ground on which to bond when a winter storm forces them together during their grounded travels to the east coast. “Ryan’s sort of an interesting case because he’s obviously like, ‘How do we market this and how do we make this sellable and profitable?’ But he loves books. There’s a big part of his heart — and they get into it in the movie — that appreciates literature, and really he just wants people to read books,” Briney said of his character, who leans more into numbers and trends. “That’s what it’s about. It’s not really about money. It’s about exposure. At least that was sort of my approach to it. title: Is Vanity Fair's Hit Piece on Taylor Swift Really Journalism?
summary: Debate over celebrity journalism highlights growing need for media literacy and strategic PR for high-profile performers.
content: After word hit the street some days back that Vanity Fair was imminently going to publish an extensively reported hit piece on music’s biggest superstar, there was some anticipation that Monday might turn out to be a bad day for Taylor Swift . Instead, it was just a bad day for journalism. As attention-seeking magazine articles go, it’s hard to remember one that landed with quite such an unanticipated — but very loud — thud as “The Mastermind,” which has even hardened anti-Swifties wondering whether May Jeong slipped it through without editorial oversight, sneaking an alleged year’s worth of work onto the internet in the dead of morning. The alternative scenario was unthinkable. You would have to imagine that the author had actually been encouraged by editors to puzzle readers with a reported op-ed in which the subject of the piece — apparently, some top-tier celebrity! — is never named, yet still is subject to accusations that she picks her own friends, harbors ambitions, owned three pairs of Ugg boots while posing as a teenage commoner, and, most slanderously, was actually popular in school. When was the last time a high-profile magazine piece got ratio-ed this badly? That would have been one year and one week ago, when an exclusive excerpt from Olivia Nuzzi’s memoir, “American Canto,” was released to an incredulous world. And if there’s something that feels a little bit familiar about Jeong’s oddball tactic of not naming names in her piece (or at least not the big ones), it’s because this “you know who it’s about, but we’re not gonna say anyway” technique was a weird conceit last grafted into big-time American journalism by Nuzzi. That author referred to RFK only as “the Politician,” her ex-boyfriend as “the man I did not marry,” and so on. Nuzzi walked so that Jeong could run. title:
Oscars: 38 Animated Movies, 104 International Films and 190
 Documentaries Make the Eligibility Lists, Setting New Records
summary: The Academy sets record eligibility slates for animation, international, and documentary, expanding nomination competition and exposure opportunities.
content: The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences has released the lists of films eligible for animated feature, documentary feature and international feature at the 99th Academy Awards, and two of the three are setting records. Animated feature has 38 eligible films, the most in the category’s history. International feature has 104, also a record. Documentary feature comes in at 190. Pixar’s “ Toy Story 5 ” and Universal and Illumination’s “The Super Mario Galaxy Movie” lead a group of studio billion-dollar tentpoles that also includes “Minions & Monsters,” “Tangles” and “Wildwood.” They come alongside Ketchup Entertainment’s “Coyote vs. Acme,” a movie plenty of people wondered if they’d ever get to see, and the return of a familiar property with GKids’ “Shaun the Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom.” Related Stories UFC's Event Sellout Spree Powers TKO Q3 Earnings WWE, Disney Team for 'Avengers: Doomsday'-Themed Worlds Collide, John Cena Classic Don’t overlook the international animated titles that have demonstrated pockets of support. Japan enters the race with “Cosmic Princess Kaguya!,” “All You Need Is Kill” and “Mobile Suit Gundam Hathaway: The Sorcery of Nymph Circe,” while Mexico offers the stop-motion feature “I Am Frankelda” and Spain brings “Decorado.” The Academy notes that some still need to complete their required theatrical runs and meet the category’s other rules before they can advance. Animation branch members vote automatically for the five nominees. Members of other branches can opt in, as long as they meet a minimum viewing requirement. Animated features can also compete in other categories, best picture included, and a country’s official international feature submission can be considered for animated feature. On the documentary side, the 190 films cover just about everything: music, politics, art, sports and true crime. The contenders include “Knife: The Attempted Murder of Salman Rushdie,” “Ask E. title:
'Cliff Booth' Star Elizabeth Debicki on Slapping Brad Pitt, 'The Movie
 Critic,' and the Rom-Com Question
summary: Elizabeth Debicki discusses career choices, working with top directors, and openness to rom-coms amid new project talks.
content: Don’t let the title fool you: “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” might offer up a breezy, very fun-to-watch new entry into the life and times of titular (and fictitious) Hollywood stuntman, but co-star Elizabeth Debicki steals the show in David Fincher’s film (in addition to stealing the heart of Brad Pitt’s Cliff). Is it time to greenlight “The New Adventures of Karen Crosby”? We think so. The much-anticipated sequel to Quentin Tarantino’s “Once Upon in Hollywood” picks up nearly a decade after the Oscar-winning antics of the previous film , finding Cliff pursuing new professional endeavors (film projecting! bartending! contract killing, kind of!). Stunt work? Eh, only when he feels like, and he certainly feels like after taking an unexpected meeting with Hollywood agent Karen Crosby (Debicki), whose grace and good humor instantly delight both Cliff and the audience. Related Stories Shawn Levy and 21 Laps Set Overall Film Deal at Sony Pictures Steven Spielberg Directing His First Western with Paul Thomas Anderson Writing the Script Tossed together by the wacky demands of Karen’s marquee client, actor Charlie Nelson (Scott Caan), the shaggy, Tarantino-penned “ Cliff Booth ” meanders its way through every corner of Hollywood, finding real emotional ballast and crackling chemistry every time Pitt and Debicki share the screen. Characteristically wordy and dense, we learn plenty about Karen along the way (including her early forays into film criticism and her current feelings about movies), and she wins Cliff’s heart by, well, literally and physically slapping the crap out of him. title: Inside the Macy’s Thanksgiving Parade at 100: Massive Minions, K-Pop Stars and ‘Sorcerer’s Apprentice’ Mickey Mouse
summary: Macy’s Parade centennial features high-profile live performance slots and TV exposure, offering performers visibility and brand partnerships.
content: The 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade is just two days away. Each year, thousands line the streets and millions more tune in around the country to watch the iconic balloons, floats and performers parade through New York City. Titled “The Greatest Celebration,” this year’s event promises to go all out, featuring more balloons and brand-new floats among the festivities. It takes months of preparation and a village of creatives working behind the scenes to bring everything together. Variety has spent the last few months speaking with the team behind the magic and going inside the epic operation of the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade. Related Stories UFC's Event Sellout Spree Powers TKO Q3 Earnings WWE, Disney Team for 'Avengers: Doomsday'-Themed Worlds Collide, John Cena Classic The floats are built in New Jersey at Macy’s Studios in Moonachie. The costumes and balloons are designed and also built. As the countdown begins, the balloons are tested, the rehearsals go into full effect and the finishing touches are added to the floats, while organizers appeal to the weather gods. But this is a well-oiled machine of artists who come prepared for the occasion. The parade debuted in 1924. This year, as it celebrates its 100th edition, Brendan Kennedy, director of creative production at Macy’s Studio, explains the heart of the parade begins with one thing: “storytelling.” When Variety caught up with Kennedy, he was already knee-deep in the design process and counting down to the big day. At this stage of planning, Kennedy and his team were collaborating with new partners and finalizing designs. The floats and balloons were in various stages of development — some still in the concept phase. “This time last year, I was starting on our first balloon for this year and we’ve been chipping away at that design-wise,” Kennedy explains. “This is just one part of the parade. There are so many aspects to it.” Kennedy noted that the team constantly pushes the boundaries of creativity, a

title: Colin Farrell: For Emma Fogarty, Who Means the World to Me
summary: Colin Farrell spotlights advocacy work honoring Emma Fogarty, underscoring philanthropy’s role in an actor’s public profile.
content: The Irish actor writes about his pal “Em,” a woman living with the rare genetic condition epidermolysis bullosa (EB). Their special bond is captured in “The Slightest Touch,” a new documentary premiering Nov. 25 on HBO Max. I met my friend Emma Fogarty nearly 16 years ago. I was sat beside her at a dinner table on an evening purposed to raise awareness for those who have the same punishing condition Emma was born with: epidermolysis bullosa (EB), a rare genetic disorder where the slightest touch or even friction of material rubbing against her skin can cause blistering and open wounds, as the skin struggles to heal. At this stage in her life, Emma’s body is 60-80% open wound. Related Stories Here's How to Watch WWE Crown Jewel 2026 Live Online UFC's Event Sellout Spree Powers TKO Q3 Earnings When she was born, the doctors told her mother and father — Pat and Malachy — that they would be better off leaving her in the hospital as she wouldn’t survive the week. What the doctors failed to diagnose was Emma’s spirit, its beauty, its utter fortitude — and that of her parents, too. Today Emma is 42, which makes her Ireland’s longest-surviving person with epidermolysis bullosa, and accompanied by constant pain. She lives in fear of cancers, which afflict those with EB in staggering numbers (she is a two-time cancer survivor). But she also lives a life filled with joy, love, meaning and friendship. She has been a wonderful friend to me over these years, providing laughter and support, adventure and her own brand of hard-earned wisdom. A few years back, I’d mentioned to Emma in passing that we should do a marathon together someday; I’d push her if she fancied. A year after my half-hearted offer, she texted me saying, “Do you remember you mentioned the marathon?” Emma had a dream that I would push her the last 4K of the Dublin City Marathon to mark her 40th birthday, with each kilometer representing a decade of her life that she’d stubbornly refused to let EB dictate. And so…

title: ‘Hooters: The Movie’ Sets Owen Patrick Joyner, Kyle Clark & Audrey Trullinger

content: EXCLUSIVE: Hooters: The Movie is officially open for business, meaning cameras are rolling in the Tampa Bay, Florida area with Owen Patrick Joyner , Kyle Clark and Audrey Trullinger starring in the origin story of the chicken wing chain. What begins as a spontaneous road trip to Clearwater Beach in pursuit of Diane (Trullinger), a young woman Ted first spots in a spring break commercial, turns into an adventure neither friend could have anticipated with Diane becoming the very first Hooters Girl. Tampa Bay is where the first Hooters restaurant opened in 1983. title: ‘The Odyssey’, ‘Widow’s Bay’ Among Top Nominees For AARP’s Movies & TV For Grownups Awards
summary: AARP's Movies for Grownups nominations spotlight mature-audience projects, boosting visibility and awards momentum for seasoned actors.
content: The Odyssey , Wild Horse Nine , The Invite, Being Heumann, and Tender Loving Care are the top nominees for Best Movie For Grownups in today’s announcement of this year’s contenders for the upcoming Movies & TV for Grownups Awards. Tom Cruise, John Malkovich, Matt Damon, Andrew Scott, and John Turturro make up the list for Best Actor and all are considered strong bets when Oscar nominations are announced in January. The big difference with the list compiled by AARP for their awards is eligible candidates must be 50 or over. Scott literally just squeaked into eligibility this year. Nominees for Best Actress are Julianne Moore, Sophie Okonedo, Marion Bailey, Meryl Streep, and Helen Mirren. Related Stories News 'The Odyssey' Leads Critics Choice Awards Below-The-Line Shortlists With 11; 'Dune: Part Three' And 'La Bola Negra' Get 8 Each News 'Cameron Winter' Shines In Vibrant Indie Weekend, 'Elsinore' Opens Strong -- Specialty Box Office The organization also hands out a few awards in TV as well with The Diplomat, DTF St. Louis, Hacks, The Pitt , and Widow ‘s Bay on the list for Best Series or Limited Series. Watch on Deadline “This year’s nominees are proof that experience is one of the most powerful creative forces in film and television,” said Dr. Myechia Minter-Jordan, CEO of AARP. “From legends like Meryl Streep and Helen Mirren to acclaimed creators like Christopher Nolan and Chris Rock, these artists are doing some of the best work of their careers and reminding audiences and the industry alike that great stories have no age limit.” Hosted by five-time Emmy winner Jane Lynch, The AARP Movies & TV for Grownups Awards will take place on Saturday, January 9, 2027, at the Beverly Wilshire, Beverly Hills. It will be broadcast on PBS, Great Performances Friday, February 26, 2027.

title:
Rian Johnson Leaves the Door Open to Star Wars Return: 'It's a World I
 Deeply Love'
summary: Rian Johnson expressed interest in returning to Star Wars, signaling potential future casting opportunities in that franchise.
content: Rian Johnson isn’t writing a Star Wars movie, but he isn’t ruling one out, either. Responding to a question from IndieWire during an in-conversation event at the 23rd Marrakech International Film Festival, the writer/director of “ Star Wars : The Last Jedi ” was clear that his next project lies elsewhere: “I’m already writing the next thing I’m going to do, and it’s not a Star Wars thing, or in that genre,” he said. “I’m very much enjoying just making my own stuff, but I mean, if the opportunity presented itself,” Johnson said, nodding. “It’s a world I deeply love. It’s also a group of people I love.” “I love Star Wars more now than I ever have,” he added. “And it’s exciting to me that there are a lot of different voices now taking cracks at it.” The timing is hard to ignore. Related Stories Jane Fonda on Documentary ‘Gaslit,’ Trump, and What the Democrats’ Midterm Victory Means for Climate Change Paul Thomas Anderson’s ‘Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall’ Getting Nationwide Release in January Johnson’s remarks land just as Lucasfilm appears to be turning back toward the corner of the saga he helped shape. Polygon reported that two long-gestating features, “Star Wars: New Jedi Order” and an untitled film from Dave Filoni , are still listed as in development by Production Weekly , despite months of silence and the soft box office performance of “The Mandalorian & Grogu.” “New Jedi Order” would theoretically bring back actress Daisy Ridley as Rey roughly 15 years after “The Rise of Skywalker,” rebuilding the Jedi Order that “The Last Jedi” so memorably called into question. Sharmeen Obaid-Chinoy is attached to direct, with George Nolfi now writing after earlier drafts from Damon Lindelof and Justin Britt-Gibson, and a stint by Bond 26 screenwriter Steven Knight . The film was pulled from its December 17, 2027 release date in May 2025.
